findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The observer mostly fails closed. It grades results as exact once per file and full name, checks the fixed file set and the aggregate report, signs records with an HMAC (keyed hash), verifies them read-only, and projects ticket fields semantically. One error blocks approval: a unit test meant to prove that a same-named result in another file gets no credit cannot catch that bug. The test only renames a file, so the fixed-file-set check rejects it first. If the grader stopped keying results by file, every named check would still pass. The warnings below cover how accurate the recorded evidence is, whether canonical ordering is deterministic, and how complete the audit exemption is.

packages/cli/tests/bounded-observation.test.ts, 'does not credit a same-named result in another file': the test appends '.foreign' to a file name. That makes the report's file set differ from fixedFiles, so gradeReport throws at the 'Incomplete fixed file set' check before any assertion matching runs. The test cannot detect the behavior it names. Suppose the results map in contract.ts were keyed only by fullName, or nodePath.resolve(file.name) were dropped from the key. A required assertion that is missing from its own file could then be satisfied by a same-named passing assertion in another fixed file. R2 says missing or ambiguous required results must refuse, so this would be a false observed success, and every unit check and the positive integration proof would still pass. Fix: keep the fixed file set intact. Remove the required assertion from its owning file, add an identically named passing assertion to a different fixed file, and assert the exact-once refusal.

bounded-observation.test.ts, 'refuses a failed suite even when every required assertion passed': the pushed '/unexpected' file also fails the fixed-file-set check first. The `file.status === 'failed'` condition in gradeReport is never exercised. Real reports would still be refused through success/numFailedTestSuites, so this is weak supporting proof, not a shipped gap. Mark one of the fixed files as failed instead.

contract.ts canonical() sorts keys with localeCompare, which depends on the process's ICU locale. Observation and verification each compute canonical() for HMAC tags and for digests such as source:tracked. If the locale differs between runs, authentication or currency can fail spuriously. This fails closed, but it contradicts the 'Deterministic authentication' comment. Use plain code-unit comparison (`left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0`).

tools.ts controlledEnvironment symlinks bin/<tool> to the resolved path in the ORIGINAL checkout, for example root node_modules/.bin/codex. bin comes first on PATH, so the run executes the original checkout's codex launcher and platform package. executionToolDetails still records execution_path as the clone path. The bytes match because the dependency trees are compared, but the retained 'actual resolved inputs' misstates which file ran, and execution reaches back into the original checkout despite the isolation decision. Either link tools under the root to their clone copies, or record the path that actually ran.

identity.ts projectedFile exempts every audit-ticket line from '## Work Log' up to the next line starting with '## '. A top-level '# ' heading, or any later content that isn't an h2, stays exempt and unbound. The plan also requires rejecting malformed or duplicate frontmatter keys and byte-binding any listed audit output that execution actually loads. Neither is enforced here: the exemption is unconditional and relies on parseTicketMetadata, which is outside this packet. Add a negative control showing the fixed lane does not load these tickets.

index.ts observeBoundedDelivery calls mkdtempSync(work), git rev-parse HEAD and runtimeIdentity() before the try/finally. If any of these throws, the temporary work directory leaks, and the reserved attempt directory has no start record or diagnostic. Verification then fails with a raw ENOENT instead of the named 'incomplete' recovery. Move them inside the try block.

index.ts derives status as interrupted from `problem.includes('interrupted')`. A timeout is also labeled interrupted, and any other error whose text contains that word, such as an assertion full name quoted in a refusal message, would be misclassified. Carry an explicit interrupted flag or a typed error instead.

The handlers ignore surplus operands: observe never inspects invocation.operands, and verify uses only operands[0]. The fixed-request refusal (CLI_ARGUMENT_INVALID for --command) therefore depends on catalog/parser wiring that is not in this packet. The fixture asserts it, but this review cannot confirm it.

After the run, the original-checkout inputs are compared before the HEAD check. If HEAD advances with a semantic change, the error is 'Changed input …' rather than the scenario's 'Candidate advanced' message. Observation is still refused correctly; only the diagnostic differs.
